mcqs.q: Proper proximal contacts and contours help to:
opts: Prevent food impaction and distribute masticatory forces
mcqs.explain: Proper contacts/contours prevent food impaction, prevent periodontal problems and caries, stabilize the arches, and distribute masticatory forces.

mcqs.q: Loss of a proper proximal contact most directly predisposes to:
opts: Food impaction with periodontal problems and caries
mcqs.explain: A poor contact allows food impaction between teeth, leading to periodontal problems and recurrent caries.

mcqs.q: Matricing is defined as creating a temporary wall:
opts: Opposite the axial walls lost during preparation
mcqs.explain: Matricing creates a temporary wall opposite the axial walls, surrounding the tooth structure lost during preparation.

mcqs.q: The PRIMARY objective of a matrix is to:
opts: Restore anatomic contours and contact areas
mcqs.explain: The primary objective of the matrix is to restore anatomic contours and contact areas.

mcqs.q: Which is an ideal requirement of a matrix?
mcqs.explain: Ideal requirements include rigidity, versatility, restoration of contour/contact, prevention of overhang, and ease of application/removal.

mcqs.q: 'Versatility' of a matrix band means it should:
opts: Adapt to almost any size and shape of tooth
Be permanently rigid in one shape
mcqs.explain: Versatility means the band can adapt to almost any size and shape of tooth.

mcqs.q: Preventing 'gingival excess' refers to avoiding:
opts: An overhang at the gingival margin
mcqs.explain: An ideal matrix prevents gingival excess (overhanging margin) at the gingival floor.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised matrix system?
mcqs.explain: Matrix systems include the universal (Tofflemire), pre-contoured/sectional, automatrix, and celluloid/polyester strips.

mcqs.q: The Universal matrix is also known as the:
mcqs.explain: The universal matrix is the Tofflemire matrix (after B.R. Tofflemire).

mcqs.q: The Tofflemire matrix has two parts:
opts: A matrix retainer and a matrix band
mcqs.explain: The Tofflemire consists of a matrix retainer (to hold the band) and the matrix band.

mcqs.q: A disadvantage of the Tofflemire band is that:
opts: The flat band must be contoured before use
It is too rigid to place
mcqs.explain: The flat Tofflemire band must be contoured (e.g. burnished with an egg burnisher on a paper pad) to achieve proper convexity.

mcqs.q: Which matrix is considered the best way to achieve a strong Class II contact?
mcqs.explain: The sectional (pre-contoured) matrix is the best way to achieve a strong contact point in Class II composites.

mcqs.q: The function of the separating RING in a sectional system is to:
opts: Adapt the sectional matrix in the cervical area (and separate the teeth)
mcqs.explain: The ring adapts the sectional matrix cervically and provides separation; V-shaped tines allow wedging from both sides.

mcqs.q: Celluloid / polyester (mylar) strips are mainly used for:
opts: Class III/IV anterior restorations (clear, allow light curing)
mcqs.explain: Clear celluloid/polyester strips are used for anterior Class III/IV composites and transmit curing light.

mcqs.q: A purpose of the WEDGE is to:
opts: Adapt the matrix to the gingival margin and prevent overhang
mcqs.explain: The wedge adapts the matrix to the gingival margin (preventing overhang), separates the teeth and stabilises the band.

mcqs.q: Wedge-induced separation of the teeth is important because it:
opts: Compensates for matrix-band thickness, giving a tight final contact
Removes the need for a matrix
mcqs.explain: Slight separation compensates for the thickness of the matrix band so that a tight contact remains after the band is removed.

mcqs.q: Wedges are commonly made of:
mcqs.explain: Wedges are typically wooden or plastic, in round or triangular (anatomic) shapes.

mcqs.q: A triangular (anatomic) wedge is preferred when the gingival margin is:
opts: Deep, to better adapt to the gingival contour
mcqs.explain: Triangular/anatomic wedges adapt better to deeper gingival margins; round wedges suit shallower margins.

mcqs.q: The wedge is usually inserted from the:
mcqs.explain: The wedge is inserted from the larger embrasure, which is usually the lingual embrasure.

mcqs.q: The matrix band shown adapted to a Class II preparation primarily restores the:
opts: Missing proximal (axial) wall, contour and contact
mcqs.explain: The matrix forms the missing proximal/axial wall, re-establishing contour and contact for the restoration.

mcqs.q: The automatrix differs from the Tofflemire in that it:
opts: Uses a band with its own lock and needs no retainer
mcqs.explain: The automatrix is a retainerless system — the band has an integral locking mechanism, so no separate retainer is needed.

mcqs.q: Why does a Tofflemire band need contouring before placement?
opts: To achieve a convex contour and proper proximal adaptation
mcqs.explain: The flat band is burnished to a convex contour so the restoration reproduces proper proximal contour and contact.

saqs.q: Why are proper proximal contacts and contours important?
saqs.a: They prevent food impaction, prevent periodontal problems/caries, stabilise the arches and distribute masticatory forces.

saqs.q: Define matricing and its primary objective.
saqs.a: Creating a temporary wall opposite the lost axial walls; primary objective = restore anatomic contour and contact.

saqs.q: List four ideal requirements of a matrix.
saqs.a: Rigidity, versatility, restores contour/contact, prevents overhang (and easy to apply/remove).

saqs.q: Give the parts and disadvantage of the Tofflemire matrix.
saqs.a: Parts = retainer + band; disadvantage = the flat band must be contoured.

saqs.q: What advantage does the sectional matrix give, and what is the ring for?
saqs.a: It gives a strong Class II contact; the ring adapts the matrix cervically and separates the teeth.

saqs.q: State the purposes of a wedge and where it is inserted.
saqs.a: Adapts the matrix gingivally (prevents overhang), separates teeth, stabilises the band; inserted from the larger (lingual) embrasure.
